BEFORE THE PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
                               OF THE STATE OF MISSOURI

In the Matter of Evergy Metro, Inc. d/b/a Evergy                        )
Missouri Metro’s Request for Authority to Implement                     )        File No. ER-2026-0143
a General Rate Increase for Electric Service                            )

STAFF MOTION FOR LEAVE TO SUPPLEMENT INITIAL BRIEF AND EXPEDITED TREATMENT

           COMES NOW the Staff (“Staff”) of the Missouri Public Service Commission

    (“Commission”), by and through counsel, and for its Motion for Leave to Supplement Initial

    Brief respectfully states as follows:

           1.     On November 6, 2026, Staff filed its Initial Brief in this proceeding.

           2.     Staff discovered that it inadvertently omitted from its Initial Brief its argument

    addressing Issue 33(A), which asked “Should the Critical Peak Rate recommended by

    Staff be implemented?”

           3.     Staff respectfully requests leave to supplement its Initial Brief with the following:

Issue 33(A) Staff Recommends the Commission Adopt the Staff-Proposed Critical Peak Rate
(“CPR”).

As stated by Ms. Lange, the CPR has existed as an idea at this Commission for almost two

decades, at least. 1 Staff took a minimalist approach in developing its CPR, which makes it

flexible for modification – and Staff is open to Commission input. 2 While conservation is one

aspect of the CPR, Ms. Lange notes that the targets of the CPR are to: 1). improve customer

understanding of what is going on in the wholesale market; and 2). give customers an

economic signal to do what they can safely do to save on their bill now and in the future. 3

  Official Transcripts, Volume 9, pg. 18, lines 23-25.

                                                           1
         4.    The limited nature of this supplemental motion corrects an inadvertent

omission, and presents Staff’s arguments concerning an issue already before

the Commission.

        5.    Staff requests that the Commission consider this portion relating to Issue 33(A)

as part of Staff’s Initial Brief. The addition would supplement Staff’s brief at page 120.

        6.    Due to the reply briefs in this proceeding being due no later than

November 18, 2026, Staff further requests expedited treatment regarding this motion

no    later   than   Friday,   November     13,    2026,   pursuant    to   Commission       Rule

20 CSR 4240-2.080(14). This pleading was filed as soon as possible, in the interest of justice

and without intent to delay these proceedings.

      WHEREFORE, Staff respectfully requests leave from the Commission to supplement

its Initial Brief regarding Issue 33(A), and any such other and further relief as the Commission

deems just and reasonable.

                                                           Respectfully submitted,
